hits.hook: 'Trying out this whole pencil business': an AI filmmaker posting a hand-drawn piece pulled 29.6K views, 1.5K likes and 169 replies, his best post of the day.
hits.video_tip: Film a 20s time-lapse of you sketching one frame of your next AI short by hand, then hard-cut to the finished AI shot of the same frame.
hits.draft_en:

First attempt below.

hits.text: Been thinking about learning how to pick up a pencil lately. Any advice?
hits.original_en: Been thinking about learning how to pick up a pencil lately. Any advice?
hits.hook: A one-line question with no media ('learning how to pick up a pencil... Any advice?') drew 19.6K views and 158 replies: asking the audience for advice turned followers into commenters.
hits.video_tip: Pair the question with a 5s clip of a blank sketchbook page and a pencil, so the post has a visual and still invites advice.
hits.draft_en:
Spending less time on AI filmmaking prompts and more time wondering about drawing by hand.

Where should someone start? Tips welcome.

virals.name: Sadhna
virals.text:
10 OPEN-SOURCE GITHUB REPOS FOR CREATING YOUR OWN AI VIDEO STUDIO

You no longer need a massive production setup to start experimenting with cinematic visuals.

These 10 repositories can help you generate videos, animate images, edit footage, and create immersive 3D environments.

1. ComfyUI
Create custom workflows for AI image, video, and audio generation.

2. Wan 2.2
Generate realistic videos from text prompts and images.

3. LTX-Video
Experiment with open video-generation models for faster creative workflows.

4. AnimateDiff
Turn static images into animated scenes using diffusion models.

5. VideoCrafter
Explore text-to-video and image-to-video generation.

6. Open-Sora
Explore open-source models and workflows for video generation.

7. HunyuanVideo
Create AI-generated video clips from text descriptions.

8. MoviePy
Automate video editing, captions, transitions, and audio with Python.

9. Blender
Build 3D environments, animate objects, and render cinematic scenes.

10. Nerfstudio
Reconstruct 3D environments from photos and video footage.

The interesting part is how these tools can work together.

Generate a scene, animate it, edit the footage, and bring everything into a 3D environment.

A complete creative workflow can start with open-source software.

🔖 Save this list and explore what you can create.

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
